Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the LuminaTech Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to LuminaTech’s Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Mark Olsen, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Mark Olsen.

Mark Olsen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our gross margin presented a mixed picture. While exhibiting stability quarter-over-quarter, the year-over-year comparison reveals a more complex narrative. Gross margin remained relatively stable at 15.3% in Q2 2019, consistent with the 15.3% recorded in Q1 2019. While overall revenue grew slightly by 2% QoQ from TWD 35.8 billion in Q1 to TWD 36.5 billion in Q2, the composition of revenue shifted. We observed a stronger contribution from our higher-margin "Advanced Solutions" segment, which grew by 8% QoQ, partially offsetting a 3% decline in the lower-margin "Legacy Products" segment. This suggests initial success from our targeted sales initiatives focused on promoting higher-value offerings. Our COGS management initiatives, particularly the "Project Phoenix" supply chain optimization program, yielded modest benefits. We achieved a 1% reduction in raw material costs, primarily through renegotiated contracts with key suppliers. However, these gains were largely offset by increased logistics expenses due to tariffs imposed on imported components from China, impacting our US market segment in particular. The implementation of our new "Smart Factory" initiative at our Taoyuan manufacturing facility contributed to a 0.5% improvement in production efficiency. This initiative, focused on automation and data analytics, reduced waste and improved throughput. However, the full benefits of "Smart Factory" are not expected to be realized until Q4 2019. Compared to Q2 2018, gross margin more than doubled, reaching TWD 5.65 billion in Q2 2019, representing a 15.7% gross margin. This substantial increase reflects that overall revenue increased by 12% YoY from TWD 32.6 billion in Q2 2018 to TWD 36.5 billion in Q2 2019. This growth was driven by strong demand for our "Advanced Solutions" in the APAC region, specifically in the telecommunications and industrial automation sectors. A strategic pivot away from low-margin, commodity-based products in 2018 significantly impacted our revenue mix. While legacy product sales declined, the focus on higher-value solutions boosted overall profitability. In Q2 2018, legacy product sales were at TWD 15 billion, while in Q2 2019, it went down to TWD 11 billion. Advanced Solutions on the other hand, went from TWD 17.6 billion to TWD 25.5 billion in the same period. Increased demand for our "Advanced Solutions" allowed us to exercise greater pricing power. The average selling price (ASP) for these solutions increased by 5% YoY, contributing significantly to the improved gross margin. This increase was particularly evident in our software and service-based offerings. Favorable currency fluctuations, particularly the appreciation of the US dollar against the Taiwanese dollar, had a positive impact on our export revenues, contributing approximately 0.7 percentage points to the gross margin improvement. Despite the strong Q2 performance, the first six months of 2019 saw a 30% decline in gross margin to TWD 7.9 billion, compared to TWD 11.3 billion in the first six months of 2018. This decline is primarily attributable to a weak Q1 performance, which was particularly challenging, with gross margins significantly impacted by increased raw material costs, supply chain disruptions due to the Lunar New Year holidays, and a weaker-than-anticipated demand in the European market. We have been aggressively investing in research and development (R&D) and sales and marketing initiatives to support the launch of our next-generation "Quantum Computing" platform. These investments, while crucial for long-term growth, have temporarily impacted our profitability in the short term. The sales cycle for our "Advanced Solutions" can be lengthy, particularly for large enterprise clients. While we saw strong demand in Q2, some of these deals are not expected to close until the second half of the year. In our Q1 2019 earnings call, we projected a gross margin of 16.5% for Q2 2019. The actual gross margin of 15.7% represents a shortfall of 0.8 percentage points. This miss can be attributed to several factors, including underestimation of the tariff impact, delayed "Project Phoenix" benefits, and an unexpected product mix shift.

We also continued to drive improvements through our operating margin performance. Our operating income for the quarter stood at TWD 1.76 billion, translating to an operating profit margin of 4.9%. The 4.9% operating margin represents a slight decrease of 0.3 percentage points compared to Q2 2024, when we reported a 5.2% operating margin. This dip can be attributed to a confluence of factors, including an increased cost of key raw materials, specifically semiconductors and specialized polymers used in our high-end consumer electronics division. We experienced a 7% increase, primarily driven by ongoing supply chain disruptions resulting from geopolitical instability in Southeast Asia. We absorbed a significant portion of these costs to remain competitive in key markets, impacting our profitability this quarter. Consistent with our long-term strategic goals, we significantly ramped up our investment in Research and Development (R&D) during Q3, specifically focusing on next-generation AI integration for our automotive product line. These investments, totaling TWD 350 million this quarter alone, are crucial for maintaining our technological edge and securing future market share, but they impacted short-term profitability. The increased R&D spending reflects a 22% increase compared to Q2. Our European operations, particularly in the consumer appliance sector, experienced a seasonal slowdown during the summer months. This translated to lower sales volumes and reduced operational efficiency as factories adjusted production schedules to meet the reduced demand. This resulted in a ~3% dip in European sales, impacting the overall operating margin. Compared to Q3 2023, our operating margin of 4.9% represents an improvement of 0.7 percentage points. In Q3 2023, our operating margin was 4.2%. This positive YoY change is primarily driven by successful cost optimization initiatives, including streamlining manufacturing processes, negotiating more favorable supplier contracts, and consolidating our logistics network, which yielded approximately TWD 200 million in cost savings during Q3 2024. We witnessed robust revenue growth in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in emerging markets like India and Indonesia, fueled by increased adoption of our mobile device offerings and successful market penetration strategies. Sales in the APAC region increased by 18% compared to Q3 2023, with the higher sales volume positively impacting our operating leverage. We increased our manufacturing efficiency due to the introduction of AI-powered systems to oversee the manufacturing process. This has increased the speed and accuracy of production and reduced waste. In our Q2 2024 earnings call, we projected an operating margin of 5.1% for Q3 2024. The actual result of 4.9% falls short of this guidance by 0.2 percentage points. The variance can be primarily attributed to unforeseen currency fluctuations, particularly the strengthening of the US dollar against several emerging market currencies, which impacted our export revenues and profitability. We had not fully factored in the extent of this volatility in our prior guidance. The launch of our new premium smartphone line in North America was delayed by approximately two weeks due to unforeseen logistical challenges. This delay impacted our Q3 sales figures and, consequently, our operating margin. We now anticipate a successful launch in Q4. Our competitors have become more aggressive in their pricing strategy, resulting in a lower margin than anticipated.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our overall wafer ASP performance. This quarter, we've seen a generally stable pricing environment across our wafer portfolio. While facing inflationary pressures on input costs (raw materials, energy, labor), we've successfully navigated these challenges, leading to a slight overall ASP increase of 0.5% compared to the prior quarter. This increase is primarily attributed to a favorable product mix shift towards higher-margin advanced nodes and a successful execution of our value-based pricing strategy, emphasizing the performance and reliability advantages of our wafers. Looking ahead to next quarter (Q3), we anticipate a further 1% increase in overall wafer ASP, driven by a combination of factors. This projection accounts for a continued favorable product mix, strategic price adjustments in specific segments, and the initial impact of our new high-performance interconnect technology. We believe this modest but steady ASP growth, coupled with volume increases in key sectors, positions us well for continued revenue growth in the second half of the year. However, we are closely monitoring geopolitical tensions and potential fluctuations in currency exchange rates, as these could introduce volatility in the ASP outlook. We are also acutely aware of increased capacity coming online from competitors, particularly in mature nodes, and are proactively managing our pricing strategy to maintain market competitiveness.

Now I’ll hand it over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mark, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our net income attributable to stockholder of the parent reached TWD 1.74 billion in Q2 2019, representing a 4.8 percentage point improvement over Q1 2019's net income. This translates to a 44.9% increase in profitability compared to the TWD 1.2 billion recorded in Q1 2019. This substantial growth is attributable to a 2.5 percentage point increase in gross margin, rising from 28.5% in Q1 to 31% in Q2, primarily due to a successful cost-reduction initiative in our manufacturing facilities in Vietnam, contributing savings of approximately TWD 150 million. We also saw a favorable shift in product mix, with higher sales of our premium product line (the "Aura" series), which boasts a significantly higher margin (45% vs. 25% for our standard line). We implemented stricter controls on operating expenses, reducing SG&A (Selling, General & Administrative Expenses) by 5% sequentially, achieved through renegotiated marketing contracts (saving an estimated TWD 30 million) and streamlining administrative processes. A 15% increase in Q2 revenue in the Southeast Asian market, particularly in Indonesia and Thailand, fueled by a successful marketing campaign targeting younger consumers and a strategic partnership with a major e-commerce platform in the region, adding approximately TWD 500 million in revenue. Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) for Q2 2019 was TWD 0.15 per share, a considerable improvement from the TWD 0.10 per share recorded in Q1 2019. This increase directly reflects the improved net income performance and underscores the effectiveness of our operational initiatives.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our sales performance by segment and platform. The second quarter of 2024 witnessed a significant rebound in revenue, driven primarily by strong performance in our Asia segment and a resurgence in our Communication platform. Total revenue for the quarter reached $4.4 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Asia continues to be our dominant market, contributing 59% of total revenue in Q2, a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. Within Asia, Southeast Asia experienced the most robust growth, with a 22% increase in revenue due to successful penetration into the burgeoning e-commerce sector. China, while still a significant contributor, saw a more moderate growth rate of 8%, reflecting increased competition from local players and evolving regulatory landscapes. India's performance was solid, growing at 14%, benefiting from our strategic partnerships with local telecom providers. We are investing heavily in localizing our product offerings and expanding our distribution networks across the region. Specific initiatives include the launch of our "Asia-First" product line, tailored to the specific needs and preferences of consumers in the region, and the expansion of our cloud infrastructure in Singapore to improve service latency. Our blended gross margin for Asia stands at 42%. North America accounted for 31% of total revenue. While the region experienced a slight slowdown compared to the previous quarter, we saw a 5% year-over-year increase. This growth was primarily driven by our enterprise solutions, particularly in the healthcare and financial services sectors. We are actively working on strengthening our relationships with key channel partners and expanding our presence in the government sector. The North American market remains highly competitive, and we are focused on differentiating ourselves through superior customer service and innovative product features. We are investing in AI-driven personalization to enhance customer engagement and improve sales conversion rates. Blended gross margin for North America is at 48%, reflecting a higher concentration of premium products and services. EMEA accounted for the remaining 10% of total revenue. The region experienced a challenging quarter due to geopolitical instability and economic uncertainty. However, we saw pockets of growth in specific markets, such as Germany and the Nordic countries, driven by demand for our cybersecurity solutions. We are actively exploring strategic partnerships to expand our reach and mitigate risks in the region. We are also focusing on cost optimization measures to improve profitability. Our current blended gross margin for EMEA is at 38%. The Communication platform has been the key driver for recovery in the second quarter, now accounting for 52% of total revenue. This reflects a significant increase in demand for our unified communication solutions, particularly our cloud-based offerings. We attribute this growth to the increasing adoption of remote work and the growing need for seamless communication and collaboration tools. Our "ConnectNow" platform, which integrates voice, video, and messaging, has seen particularly strong adoption among small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). We are continuing to invest in enhancing the functionality and scalability of our Communication platform to meet the evolving needs of our customers. The platform enjoys a healthy gross margin of 55% due to its software-centric nature and high recurring revenue. Security remains a crucial component of our portfolio, accounting for 30% of total revenue. We saw strong demand for our threat detection and response solutions, driven by the increasing sophistication of cyberattacks. Our AI-powered security platform, "ShieldAI," has been gaining traction among enterprises seeking to proactively protect their networks and data. We are continuing to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the evolving threat landscape. Our partnership with DarkTrace has yielded substantial benefit in this space. The Security platform maintains a robust gross margin of 60%. Our Analytics platform contributed 18% of total revenue. While the growth rate was slightly lower compared to Communication and Security, we saw increasing adoption of our data visualization and business intelligence tools. Our "InsightHub" platform, which helps businesses analyze their data and gain actionable insights, has been particularly popular among retailers and healthcare providers. We are focused on expanding the functionality of our Analytics platform and integrating it with our other offerings. The Analytics platform has a gross margin of 50%.

And although still early, our CapEx allocation remains strategically aligned with our long-term growth objectives, holding steady at approximately TWD 1 billion. The dominant share of our CapEx, 75% or TWD 750 million, continues to be directed towards our 12-inch wafer fabrication facilities, supporting the increasing demand for advanced node semiconductors, particularly in the automotive, 5G infrastructure, and high-performance computing (HPC) sectors. A significant portion of the 12-inch CapEx is dedicated to upgrading existing equipment, including the acquisition of advanced metrology tools from KLA and Applied Materials, which are critical for improving yield rates on our 7nm and 5nm processes. We've observed a 1.8% yield improvement in our 7nm process this quarter directly attributable to these upgraded metrology tools, translating to an estimated $12 million in cost savings. Furthermore, $150 million was spent on new lithography equipment from ASML, allowing us to better handle the increasing complexity of our 5nm production. This is crucial as we prepare to ramp up production of our new AI accelerator chip. To meet the anticipated surge in demand for our advanced logic chips, primarily driven by contracts with leading hyperscale data centers, we are expanding capacity at our Fab 3 facility in Hsinchu, adding new cleanroom space and installing additional etching and deposition tools. We expect this capacity expansion to come online in Q1 2025 and contribute approximately 10% to our overall 12-inch wafer output. This allocation focuses on improving the reliability and efficiency of our 12-inch fabs, including upgrades to our power and cooling systems, as well as investments in advanced automation technologies. We are implementing AI-powered predictive maintenance algorithms across our fabs to minimize downtime and optimize equipment performance. Early results show a potential reduction in unplanned downtime by up to 15%, leading to improved operational efficiency. While the primary focus remains on 12-inch operations, we recognize the continued importance of our 8-inch facilities, particularly in supporting the mature process nodes used in power management ICs, analog devices, and microcontrollers. This allocation is primarily focused on refurbishing existing equipment in our 8-inch fabs to extend their lifespan and maintain production capacity without incurring the significant cost of new equipment, a cost-effective way to support the demand for these essential components. We are investing in process optimization and yield enhancement projects in our 8-inch fabs to improve the profitability of these operations, implementing advanced statistical process control (SPC) techniques to identify and address sources of variation in our manufacturing processes. This critical allocation supports our long-term technology roadmap, including investments in developing next-generation process technologies, such as 3nm and beyond, and in pilot lines to test and refine new manufacturing processes before they are deployed in our high-volume fabs. $40 million is allocated to the development of advanced packaging technologies like 3D stacking and fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP). These technologies are becoming increasingly important for enabling the integration of multiple chips into a single package, offering significant performance and power efficiency advantages. $60 million goes to researching new materials for use in future generations of semiconductors, including exploring alternative channel materials and high-k dielectrics to improve transistor performance.

With that, I’ll turn it to David Lee for a deeper look at operational performance.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was our gross margin performance. To address these challenges and improve our gross margin performance in the second half of 2019, we are implementing the following strategies. We are accelerating the implementation of "Project Phoenix" to realize the full benefits of supply chain optimization, including negotiating more favorable terms with suppliers, diversifying our sourcing base, and streamlining our logistics operations. We are refining our pricing strategies to better reflect the value of our products and services, including implementing dynamic pricing models, offering bundled solutions, and focusing on value-based selling. We are focusing our sales and marketing efforts on high-growth markets, such as Southeast Asia and Latin America, where demand for our "Advanced Solutions" is strong. We will continue to invest in R&D to develop innovative products and services that command premium pricing and drive long-term growth. We anticipate that these initiatives will contribute to a gradual improvement in gross margin in the second half of 2019. We are targeting a gross margin of 17.0% for Q4 2019. We will continue to closely monitor market conditions and adjust our strategies as needed to ensure that we achieve our financial objectives. The company will prioritize automation in manufacturing to decrease labor costs, and also leverage AI to optimize logistics and reduce shipping costs, particularly in the APAC region.

Additionally, our sales performance, we are pleased with the strong performance in the second quarter, which reflects the success of our strategic initiatives and the resilience of our business model. The growth in Asia and the resurgence of our Communication platform are particularly encouraging. We remain focused on investing in innovation, expanding our global reach, and delivering exceptional value to our customers. While we acknowledge the ongoing macroeconomic challenges, we are confident in our ability to navigate these headwinds and achieve our long-term growth objectives. We're also actively monitoring the impact of inflation on operating costs and are implementing measures to mitigate these pressures. Specifically, we are re-negotiating contracts with key suppliers and optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency. We are also exploring opportunities to automate certain processes to reduce labor costs. We are carefully managing our headcount and prioritizing investments in areas that will drive the most growth.

We’re also seeing early traction in our inventory management. Our Q2 ending inventory balance stood at $785 million, a decrease of 3.5% compared to $814 million in Q1 2019. While seemingly positive, this reduction is primarily driven by decreased customer demand rather than optimized supply chain efficiency. Days of Inventory (DOI) for Q2 averaged 72 days, representing a slight increase of 2 days compared to the 70 days recorded in Q1 2019. This increase, despite the inventory reduction, signals a slower sell-through rate, further corroborating the impact of macroeconomic headwinds on customer demand. While overall revenue in North America remained relatively stable, we saw a significant shift in order patterns. Customers, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors, are placing smaller, more frequent orders, reflecting a just-in-time inventory strategy. This resulted in a 6% decrease in average order size compared to Q1, but a 12% increase in the number of individual orders processed. DOI in North America mirrored the company average at 72 days. Europe presented a more challenging landscape. Continued Brexit uncertainty coupled with sluggish growth in key economies like Germany resulted in a more pronounced slowdown. Our European DOI jumped to 78 days, a 5-day increase from Q1, indicating a more significant inventory buildup due to weaker sales. We are actively working with our sales teams in Europe to offer targeted promotions and incentives to stimulate demand and reduce inventory levels. Asia-Pacific showed mixed results. While China experienced moderate growth, other markets like South Korea and Japan faced headwinds. Inventory levels in China remained manageable, but we saw an increase in slower-moving inventory in Southeast Asia, driven by over-optimistic initial forecasts for several large infrastructure projects that have been delayed. We've implemented a regional inventory redistribution program to address this imbalance, moving excess inventory from Southeast Asia to regions with higher demand. We are seeing a disproportionate impact on our high-margin product lines, with customers opting for lower-cost alternatives or delaying purchases of premium products due to budget constraints, contributing to a higher DOI for these products. We are adjusting our pricing strategy and developing targeted marketing campaigns to address this issue, focusing on highlighting the long-term cost benefits and superior performance of our premium offerings. Demand for our commodity products has remained relatively stable, albeit with thinner margins. However, even in this category, we've observed a shift towards smaller order sizes and shorter lead times, indicating a focus on minimizing inventory holding costs among our customers. To improve our visibility into customer demand and optimize our inventory levels, we are accelerating the rollout of our enhanced demand forecasting system, leveraging machine learning algorithms to better predict customer behavior. We expect this system to be fully operational by the end of Q3 2019. We are also implementing a more agile supply chain management system, allowing us to respond more quickly to changes in demand and minimize inventory holding costs. This includes closer collaboration with our key suppliers to reduce lead times and improve supply chain flexibility. We are piloting a vendor-managed inventory (VMI) program with one of our largest distributors in North America, which is showing promising results in reducing inventory levels and improving order fulfillment rates. The continued caution among our customer base underscores the need for a more conservative approach to forecasting for the second half of 2019. We are revising our revenue guidance accordingly, taking into account the increased uncertainty in the global economic environment. We are proactively managing our inventory levels by implementing targeted sales promotions, optimizing our pricing strategy, and improving our demand forecasting capabilities. We are also focusing on strengthening our relationships with key customers, providing them with tailored solutions and support to help them manage their inventory more effectively.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily Carter for the tech and product update.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our operating margin performance. We are actively addressing the aforementioned issues through the following strategies. We are actively diversifying our supply chain to mitigate the impact of geopolitical risks and raw material price fluctuations, including establishing partnerships with new suppliers in more stable regions. We remain committed to investing in R&D to maintain our technological leadership and drive future growth, believing these investments will yield significant returns in the long term. We are implementing additional cost management measures across the organization to improve operational efficiency and reduce expenses. We will continue to focus on developing and marketing high-margin products and services to improve our overall profitability, including our premium product lines and value-added services. We are increasing our hedging activities to mitigate the impact of foreign currency exchange volatility.

We’ve also support our CapEx allocation. Our CapEx investments are geographically concentrated in Taiwan, reflecting our commitment to maintaining our leadership position in the region. However, we are also closely monitoring the evolving geopolitical landscape and exploring potential opportunities for diversification in other regions, such as Southeast Asia and the United States. We're currently evaluating potential partnerships and incentives offered by various governments to support semiconductor manufacturing. The unwavering demand for advanced node semiconductors across key sectors such as AI, automotive, and 5G is the primary driver behind our continued investment in 12-inch operations. The AI sector, in particular, has experienced a surge in demand, with a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. The competitive landscape in the semiconductor industry remains intense. We are closely monitoring the investments of our competitors and adjusting our CapEx strategy accordingly. We are focused on maintaining our technological lead and offering our customers the most advanced manufacturing capabilities. Our disciplined CapEx allocation has contributed to strong financial performance in Q3 2024. We achieved a gross margin of 48%, driven by improved yields and higher average selling prices. We are confident that our CapEx investments will continue to drive profitable growth in the years to come. We are actively pursuing operational efficiencies to maximize the return on our CapEx investments, including implementing lean manufacturing principles, automating key processes, and optimizing our supply chain. We are targeting a 5% reduction in operating costs by the end of 2025.

And finally, on our inventory levels, looking ahead, we expect the cautious inventory management trend to continue in the near term. However, we remain confident in our long-term growth prospects, driven by our strong product portfolio, our global reach, and our commitment to innovation. We will continue to monitor the global economic environment closely and adjust our strategy as needed to ensure that we are well-positioned to capitalize on future growth opportunities. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, slightly lower than our previous projection of $2.4 billion.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the overall wafer ASP comments, specifically regarding the competitive pressures you mentioned, and whether you anticipate those pressures to intensify in the coming quarters?

Mark Olsen:
Certainly. As we noted, we're seeing increased capacity coming online from competitors, particularly in mature nodes like 28nm and 40nm. This is primarily from players in China. We are proactively managing this pressure through a few key strategies. First, we are focusing on value-added applications in these mature nodes, such as automotive and industrial IoT, where reliability and longevity are paramount. Second, we are selectively reducing capacity in the most affected nodes and shifting resources to higher-margin opportunities. Third, we are aggressively pursuing cost optimization measures to maintain our competitiveness. While we anticipate continued pressure in mature nodes, we believe our differentiated offerings and cost management efforts will allow us to mitigate the impact. We are also closely monitoring the geopolitical landscape and potential trade restrictions, which could further impact the competitive dynamics.

Analyst 2:
On net margin and Diluted EPS, how much of the decline in year-to-date EPS is attributable to the strategic investments you mentioned, and what is the expected payback period on those investments?

Sarah Chen:
A significant portion of the year-over-year decline in net income and diluted EPS, roughly 70%, is directly linked to our strategic investments in R&D and infrastructure. Specifically, we invested TWD 2 billion in developing our next-generation AI platform, which is expected to launch in Q4 2019. While this investment impacts short-term profitability, it is crucial for maintaining our competitive edge in the long run. We project that this platform will contribute at least TWD 1 billion in additional revenue in 2020. We anticipate a payback period of approximately 2 to 3 years on these investments, with significant revenue growth and improved operational efficiencies expected in the years following the launch of the AI platform. We are also actively pursuing geographic diversification, focusing on expanding our presence in North America and Europe. We have recently signed a distribution agreement with a major retailer in the US, which will allow us to reach a wider audience. We are continuing to implement cost optimization initiatives across all areas of our business, targeting to reduce operating expenses by an additional 3% in the second half of the year. We expect EPS to rebound to at least TWD 0.45 in the second half, barring unforeseen circumstances.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to operating margin and supply chain diversification strategies?

Emily Carter:
Certainly. Our supply chain diversification efforts are focused on establishing partnerships with new suppliers in more stable regions to mitigate the impact of geopolitical risks and raw material price fluctuations. We are working closely with our engineering teams to qualify these new suppliers and ensure that their products meet our stringent quality standards. We are also investing in technology to improve our supply chain visibility and resilience. This includes implementing a blockchain-based platform to track the origin and movement of our raw materials, and developing AI-powered algorithms to predict potential supply chain disruptions. For operating margin improvements, we have new AI-driven personalization to enhance customer engagement and improve sales conversion rates.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on inventory or DOI, is this increased DOI a systemic issue, or are there specific product lines or regions driving the increase?

David Lee:
It's a combination of both, actually. While the overall cautious approach to inventory management among our customer base is systemic, reflecting the global economic uncertainty, there are specific product lines and regions that are driving a disproportionate share of the DOI increase. As I mentioned earlier, we are seeing a greater impact on our high-margin product lines, as customers are opting for lower-cost alternatives or delaying purchases of premium products due to budget constraints. Regionally, Europe is experiencing a more significant inventory buildup due to weaker sales, while Southeast Asia has seen an increase in slower-moving inventory due to delays in large infrastructure projects. We are addressing these specific issues with targeted sales promotions, regional inventory redistribution programs, and adjustments to our pricing strategy. We are also implementing a more granular approach to demand forecasting, taking into account the specific dynamics of each product line and region.

Closing

Mark Olsen:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
